answer: First, the registering agent receives a nebula of pseudo-random RAM offsets sealed under a verifier key, then must walk them in a fixed spiral order, proving each cache-line traversal by returning a cryptographic seal over the touched bytes and the prior seal. The verifier replays the walk in fresh memory and checks the seal chain; a faster-than-physical traversal implies forged locality. One mismatch fails the epoch and forfeits the bond, drowning the fake-identity signal in real cost.
